# conflict-resolver

## Quick Reference

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Audience / Role** | Architect / Orchestrator (`deep-reasoning` profile) |
| **When to Load** | Resolving merge conflicts during Phase 6 integration of parallel Executor worktrees |
| **Execution Modes Supported** | **Single-Framework Native** (parallel native worktrees) and **Multi-Framework MCP / CLI** (parallel delegated worktrees) |
| **Companion Scripts** | `bin/ai-orch`, `scripts/apply_fix_to_worktree.sh` (`task-worktree-ops`) |
| **Related Skills** | `orchestration-workflow`, `task-spec-authoring`, `task-worktree-ops`, `orchestration-metrics` |

Use this skill as the **Architect** when resolving merge conflicts in files
generated by parallel Executor tasks (delegated work dispatched in parallel worktrees that then
need merging back together during Phase 6 integration).

## Logic and Behavior

- **Context:** You are the Architect integrating parallel task branches
  during Phase 6 (`git merge --no-ff <feature-branch>`) and encounter merge
  conflicts (`<<<<<<< HEAD`).
- **Triage the Conflict Type First (Do Not Blindly "Preserve Both"):**
  - **Mechanical Conflicts** (adjacent imports, barrel/index exports,
    route/plugin registration lists, configuration keys where both tasks
    followed a disjoint spec): **combine both sides** cleanly, preserving
    ordering and formatting conventions.
  - **Task registry conflicts (`tasks/00-INDEX.md`):**
    Executor worktrees should NOT commit `tasks/00-INDEX.md` when working on an
    isolated feature branch (the orchestrator runs `sync-index --apply` on the
    integration branch after merging). If `00-INDEX.md` ever conflicts on merge,
    `ai-orch tasks sync-index --apply` (or `ai-orch tasks merge-index`) resolves it
    deterministically in one command from the task files on disk.
  - **Incompatible Design or Signature Conflicts** (two tasks changed the
    same function signature differently, introduced competing abstractions
    or duplicate type names for the same concept, or mutated the same
    control-flow block incompatibly): **STOP.** Do not stitch both designs
    together into a hybrid that compiles but ships two overlapping
    mechanisms. Pick one canonical design (or ask the user if the choice
    is an architectural fork), keep that branch's design, and **bounce the
    conflicting task back to its Executor session** to rebase/adapt against
    the chosen contract.
- **Verification (Mandatory Post-Resolution Gate):**
  - Run the linter and type-checker.
  - Run the automated **test suites of BOTH involved features** (not just one).
  - Run a **full consuming build** (Phase 5b integration gate) to catch
    duplicate exports or cross-module contract breaks that single-feature
    unit tests miss.
- **Telemetry & Spec Feedback:** If a non-trivial conflict occurred because
  parallel task specs lacked disjoint write scopes or a shared registry
  pattern, record it as a decomposition defect (see `orchestration-metrics`
  and `task-spec-authoring`) so future batches pre-assign the shared symbol
  or file section.
